evidence.thread_resolution:
thomaseizinger: At the moment there is no limit. What do you think is an appropriate limit to set here?
thomaseizinger: I've introduced a crate `futures-bounded` that I am planning to use for housing utilities around size and time bounded worker futures.
thomaseizinger: I've chosen an arbitrary limit of 100 for now but `futures_bounded::WorkerFutures` is ready to work with backpressure once we have it. For now, any additional streams will be dropped.
mxinden: `100` as a default sounds good to me.

I am afraid we will have to make this configurable. E.g. Substrate has chosen a very high `max_negotiating_inbound_streams` limit in order for `libp2p-request-response` to not hit any limits.

https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/blob/a6b0d435995d7101e70ee0aab1707d0807024a3f/client/network/src/service.rs#L472

//CC @kpp and @melekes
thomaseizinger: Those are for the overall `Swarm` though whereas here we are talking about the limit for a single protocol. We can still make it configurable though, I think adding an option here is not a breaking change. I'll look into it!
thomaseizinger: I think having to configure such a limit per protocol now is a slight decrease in usability. I still think that this is the right way forward though. Hopefully, we can figure out a more generic approach in the future.
